content.title: About
content.content: Mulligatawany soup is a fragrant Indian broth made with chicken stock, coconut milk, curry, apples, and a blend of spices. It combines sweet, spicy, and slightly tangy notes for a rich, warming flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “mulligatawany” comes from the Tamil phrase meaning “pepper water”.
Traditionally it is served with rice, but modern versions often use quinoa or barley.
Coconut milk gives the soup its characteristic creamy texture and subtle sweetness.
It is commonly garnished with fried onion strips and fresh cilantro.
In India the soup is considered to aid digestion thanks to spices like turmeric and cumin.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Turmeric and ginger provide powerful antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin C from apples and the spices boost the body’s immune defenses.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Cumin and fennel promote bile secretion and ease food breakdown.

items.title: Reduces inflammation
items.content: Turmeric’s anti‑inflammatory properties are beneficial for chronic inflammation.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Chicken and optional legumes supply essential amino acids.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some recipes include shrimp or fish; those with allergies should use only chicken.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared broth can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium levels in check.

items.title: Coconut milk and calories
items.content: Coconut milk is high in fat, so calorie‑conscious individuals should consume the soup in moderation.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Excessive chili can irritate the stomach of sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, garnished with fresh cilantro, fried onions, and a lime wedge. It pairs well with boiled rice, sourdough bread, or naan flatbreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, portion into freezer‑safe containers and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water or broth if needed.
